items.title: What this page is
items.detail:
Every live summer 2027 internship that fits a master's in biostatistics, ranked, with the apply link on each row and the close date in a tag. Open now is what you can send today. Later is what has a known window but is not posted yet. Not a fit is everything already checked and rejected, with the reason, so you do not waste time on it twice. Tick a row when you send it.

Rebuilt every night from the employers' own job systems, so a row here means the requisition was readable tonight, not that it existed last week.

items.title: Worth doing this week

**3. San Diego is opening.** Pfizer's Statistics summer program lists San Diego and takes applications until January 31; register on its site now so you can apply the day the listings post. BMS ran a Biostatistics intern in San Diego last summer and takes applications through March; set an alert. ZS lists San Diego on its analytics intern and is open now.

**4. Two remote seats pair with any city:** Amgen's graduate Data Scientist (closes November 7) and Centene's graduate Analytics intern (rolling).

**5. Still true:** you have no named contact anywhere. One recruiter or biostatistics manager at any of these employers is worth more than ten more rows.

items.title: How this field actually hires a master's student
items.detail:
Big pharma runs structured summer programmes that open between mid-September and November and often gate biostatistics seats at PhD, which is why several employers below sit in Not a fit despite looking perfect. Contract research organisations hire at volume and later, more rolling, and they are where a master's is the standard credential rather than the exception. Device companies in Southern California are the third route and the most geographically convenient. Economic and health consulting is the fourth, and it is unusual in that it states the master's eligibility openly and pays the most.

One thing the record shows clearly: employers that name a graduation window rather than a degree level are the ones you clear. Analysis Group asks for a degree completed in winter 2027 or summer 2028, and May 2028 sits inside that.

Ionis (Carlsbad, opens Feb), Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer La Jolla, Vertex, Takeda, Lilly, Acadia, Crinetics, Avidity, Janux: pharma and biotech.

**ZS**, UTC: Decision Analytics Associate intern lists San Diego; open now.

items.title: Phoenix

**Medtronic**, Tempe: large campus on the same board as Northridge.

items.title: Remote and CROs
items.detail:
IQVIA, Parexel, ICON, Syneos Health, Medpace, PPD (Thermo Fisher), Fortrea, Worldwide Clinical Trials, Precision for Medicine: contract research organizations, the highest-volume hirers of master's statisticians, mostly remote or hybrid, mostly SAS.
Cytel and Certara: statistics-first companies where an MS is the target degree; Cytel runs a statistical programming intern program.
Amgen's grad data science interns are remote (open now).
Merck (New Jersey and Pennsylvania): 2027 Future Talent interns in Biostatistics, Statistical Programming, Epidemiology/RWE and Health Economics data science, all open, all master's-eligible. Not California, listed because the titles are exactly your degree.
AstraZeneca and Regeneron have both hired Michigan MS Biostatistics interns before, per the School of Public Health.

Checked again tonight and the answer has not moved for the third time running. Genentech's entire intern programme is **four reqs, all Spring 2027, all South San Francisco laboratory work**: Cell Culture and Bioprocess Operations, Cell Line Development Automation, Pharmaceutical Technical Development Bioassay, and Product Technical Development Digital Sciences. No summer term and no statistics seat anywhere in it.

Worth knowing rather than just filtering out: Genentech was the biggest name on your Bay Area list, so this is the reason that region looks thinner for you than it did two weeks ago.

None are in your metros and none are clinical or statistical. Boston Scientific has now been checked three times with the same result.

Merck's 2027 Future Talent Program genuinely has the right roles, Biostatistics, Statistical Programmer, Epidemiology & RWE, and Quantitative Pharmacology, so they were re-read at source tonight rather than taken on trust, because two show *"2 Locations"* and one shows *"4 Locations"* without naming them.

Every location resolves to Rahway NJ, West Point PA, Upper Gwynedd PA or Boston. No California option and no remote option on any of them. All close Oct 31. If you would consider the East Coast for one summer, say so and they go straight onto the list, because on role content they are the best matches found anywhere.

No statistics, no programming, nothing that builds the record you need. Worth knowing it exists because it dates CRO hiring to now rather than spring. sections.title: Return offers: what the numbers say
sections.note: Verified = the company's own published figure or the NACE survey. Estimate = third-party guides; treat as a rough range, not a company statement.

items.title: Industry benchmark: 63% of interns converted to full-time last year
items.detail: The NACE 2026 Internship & Co-op Report puts the intern-to-full-time conversion rate at **63.1% for the 2024-25 cohort**, the highest in five years. Offer rates rose nearly 10 points and 88.3% of offers were accepted. Source: NACE, survey run Oct 2025 to Jan 2026. [NACE](https://www.naceweb.org/talent-acquisition/internships/intern-conversion-rate-hits-highest-mark-in-five-years)

items.title: Medtronic: 77% of eligible interns became full-time
items.detail: Medtronic's own newsroom: **77% of eligible interns became full-time employees** the prior year, from a program of nearly 400 interns. The strongest published number on your map, and Medtronic has sites in Northridge and Tempe. [Medtronic](https://news.medtronic.com/medtronic-summer-internship-program)

items.title: Johnson & Johnson: roughly 65 to 70% of strong interns get return offers
items.detail: Third-party internship guides put J&J's return-offer rate at 65 to 70% for high-performing interns, including leadership development program seats. J&J does not publish a figure.

items.title: Amgen: roughly 30 to 40% overall, about 75% in R&D roles
items.detail: Third-party estimates only; Amgen publishes nothing. General interns 30 to 40%, R&D and biotech-specific roles around 75%, rotational programs 85 to 90%. A biostatistics seat sits on the R&D side.

items.title: Gilead: roughly 40 to 55% receive return offers
items.detail: Third-party estimate, labeled as such by the source: 40 to 55% receive return offers and about 63% accept, from a class of 80 to 120 interns a summer. Gilead itself says interns are considered for full-time roles but publishes no rate.

items.title: Genentech, Kite, Kaiser: "priority consideration", no published rate
items.detail: Genentech: interns receive priority consideration for full-time, rotation and contract roles. Kite: consideration for full-time positions, rotation programs or contract roles. Kaiser Research & Evaluation: potential return offers or full-time referrals. None of the three publishes a number.

items.title: CROs: no published rates, but the hiring path is structural
items.detail: IQVIA, Parexel, ICON and Medpace publish no conversion figures. They hire master's-level statisticians and programmers in volume every year, so an intern who performs is usually hired into an open seat rather than competing for a rare one. Treat the lack of a number as unknown, not as bad.

items.title: How to actually get the offer
items.detail: Three things that hold across every program: say in the first two weeks that you want a return offer and ask what earns one; ship something that outlives the summer (a validated analysis, a Shiny tool, a documented dataset); and meet people on adjacent teams, because a second sponsor is often what turns a good review into an offer.

sections.title: Careers sites that have to be checked by hand
sections.note: These employers' job systems block automated reading, so nothing from them appears above unless someone looks.

items.title: Two boards came off this list tonight
items.detail:
This section exists so you know what is not being covered. It got shorter tonight for the first time.

**Analysis Group** and **IQVIA** are both readable now. Neither was ever really closed: their bot filters reject an automated script with an error but serve a normal browser, so reading them through a browser works. That is now the method for the rest of this list. It matters because roughly thirty of the sixty-three job systems on your side could not be read, and the majority of those are contract research organisations, which is the part of your market where a master's is the standard credential.

items.title: IQVIA: readable now, and it has nothing for you yet
items.detail:
The board was read in full tonight: just over a thousand open roles. Every intern position on it is outside the United States: Tel Aviv, Sofia, Shanghai, Prague, Bratislava, Dalian, Mexico City, Athens, Kuala Lumpur. There is no US biostatistics, statistical programming or clinical data internship posted.

That is a useful answer rather than a disappointing one. IQVIA has been the single biggest hole in this page for weeks and the honest reading is that their US student programme simply is not open yet. Nothing to do here now, and no reason to keep wondering.

items.title: The rest of the CROs, and this is still the expensive gap
items.detail: Medpace, Parexel, ICON, Syneos, Fortrea, Precision for Medicine, Cytel and Certara all returned nothing to tonight's sweep. These are the employers most likely to hire a master's biostatistician, they hire later and more rolling than pharma, and they are invisible here. The browser method proved on IQVIA tonight gets pointed at them next.

items.title: Pharma, biotech and device sites that returned nothing
items.detail: Neurocrine, Ionis, Edwards Lifesciences, BioMarin, Vertex, Exelixis, Denali, Guardant, AbbVie/Allergan, Masimo, Applied Medical, Regeneron, Grifols and the Xencor/Arcutis/Puma/Capsida/ImmunityBio group. Several of these are Southern California and would be the most convenient employers on the whole page, so they are worth the unblocking effort.

items.title: Hospital systems and health plans
items.detail: Kaiser Permanente Research & Evaluation, Cedars-Sinai, City of Hope, Providence, Mayo Clinic Arizona, Dignity/CommonSpirit, Molina, and the CHLA/Scripps/Salk/LJI cluster. Research institutes and hospital systems are in scope for you, so these are a real gap rather than a tidy one.

sections.title: What this page is ranking against
sections.note: Your own answers and your resume, as recorded. If any of this is wrong, say so and the ranking changes.

items.title: Sector: private industry first (pharma, then CROs and biotech); hospital systems and research institutes are fine; no government or public sector
items.detail: Public universities and their hospitals (UC, ASU) are excluded under the public-sector rule; private nonprofits like Kaiser, Cedars-Sinai, City of Hope, Mayo and Stanford Health Care are included.

items.title: Direction: clinical trials, medical devices, health analytics; avoid genomics
items.detail: Genomics companies stay on the map but rank last.

items.title: Consulting: scientific yes, strategy no
items.detail: Added September 27. Scientific and economic consulting counts, meaning firms where the work is HEOR, epidemiology, health economics or biostatistics (Analysis Group, Exponent). Strategy and management consulting does not (Guidehouse is the example). Detroit-area hospital research is in for Henry Ford specifically.

items.title: Degree: MS Biostatistics, University of Michigan, expected May 2028; BS Data Science and BS Anthropology, ASU 2026, Barrett Honors, 4.0
items.detail: May 2028 clears every enrollment gate seen so far, including "enrolled the fall after the internship" and "graduating December 2027 or later."

items.title: Skills: R and Python strong, SQL moderate, SAS in progress (class this year); Tableau, R Shiny, ggplot2, scikit-learn
items.detail: Methods on the resume: ANOVA, regression, SARIMA time series, sequence analysis, survival analysis, XGBoost. Once the SAS class is done, add it to the resume and the CRO and pharma programming seats open up.

items.title: Geography: California first, Phoenix fine, remote fine
items.detail: Areas are listed in this order: Los Angeles, Orange County, Bay Area, San Diego, Phoenix, remote.

items.title: Goal: a return offer from the internship
items.detail: See the Return offers section. Device companies publish the best numbers.
